sections.title: MINUTES OF THE REBELLION: Lumumba! Lumumba!
paragraphs:
A wild leap forward… I am naked.  
I am the boiling blood of Africa… Here I stand.  
I came with bare body… came to be shattered.  
I carry the heart of resurrection, I am Lumumba.  
You can dissolve my body in acid… I am naked.  
But you can never kill my essence… Armored, my spirit is.  
Suppressed and squeezed, the flame of honor ignited, I exploded.  
The mountain burst, the brain of the era is spewing lava,  
I carry the music of the Congo, I am Lumumba.  
I bow to the delicate ant of my country, I devour the oppressor,  
I turned the Belgian king into a worm, fittingly.  
Born in Africa for brotherhood, we are not slaves.  
The fox outside made a deal with the local servant inside,  
They stole the bread, water, and light of my country,  
They spilled the dreams’ blood onto the noble land of Congo.  
I ventilated the underground of the dark continent with my hands.  
I registered my name in the book of revolutionary martyrs,  
With a determined life pulse, I rammed my name to the stone,  
I engraved myself, at the forefront, at the very beginning.  
Patrice Emery Lumumba, forget this name.  
But never forget the name of the collaborator Mobutu.  
If a poet has the right to speak, I request a place,  
Earthly valor, on behalf of the divine children of Africa.  
We took the floor to complete a half-sentence:  
Lumumba, a naked arrival, a naked departure.  
Stretch your ribs, children, we are late!

footnotes.text: The poem was translated from Turkish into English by Onurcan Balcı and Furkan Çirkin.
